technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Boot's standard auto-configuration mechanism for the singlenode binder (U7).
Implement an in-memory, pluggable test binder that mirrors the production binder API so existing message-handling code can be exercised without an external bus (U1).
Provide Hamcrest-based matchers as the idiomatic assertion style for the new test support (U1).
For the trigger module migration, reuse the existing s-c-s source module conventions and re-implement any XD-specific dependencies on top of the s-c-s APIs (U3).
For Redis/Sentinel cluster support, leverage Spring Data Redis with Lettuce (cluster-aware topology) and reuse s-c-s binder abstractions; add a `cluster` profile to existing configuration (U4).
For YARN distributed deployment, treat U2 as an investigation/proof-of-concept (SPI + YARNModuleDeployer strategy document + minimal prototype), not a full production implementation (U2).

For YARN container parameters, pass module definition parameters via the existing YARN container launch context (env/system properties consumed by the module on startup) rather than introducing a new IPC channel (U8).
Receptor-client upgrade (U5) follows the upstream Receptor API semver-aware migration path; no behavioural changes are introduced beyond the new API surface.
Admin UI work (U6) is configuration-only: wire the existing admin UI client module to the spring-cloud-data server profile; no UI code changes.
assumptions: One productive workday equals 8 hours of focused development by a single experienced Java/Spring developer.
The developer is already familiar with Spring Framework 6.x, Spring Boot, Spring Cloud Stream and Spring Cloud Data Flow conventions.
A working local dev environment, Maven/Gradle build, CI, and reference deployments (Redis, Rabbit, YARN testbed) are already available.
U2 (YARN distributed deployment) is treated as an investigation plus a working prototype/SPI, not a fully production-hardened deployer.
U6 only requires server-side configuration plus minor client wiring; no new UI screens or backend endpoints are built.
Trigger module functionality to be ported in U3 is small/medium in scope (timer-based source) and does not require redesign.
Redis cluster (U4) work uses Spring Data Redis cluster topology; custom sharding logic is out of scope.
All 8 user stories are taken at face value; no hidden cross-cutting refactors beyond what's stated are included.
Integration testing and minor bug fixing at the end is included as a single activity.

activities.activity_name: Overall requirements analysis and technical design
activities.activity_description: Review the 8 user stories, produce an integrated design covering the test framework, YARN SPI prototype, trigger module port, Redis cluster support, receptor-client upgrade, admin UI wiring, singlenode auto-config and YARN container parameters, and align with existing s-c-s/s-c-d module conventions.
Design the public API for the new test support in s-c-s: TestSupport binder entry points, configuration property binding test utilities, and assertion entry points integrated with Hamcrest.
Implement an in-memory, in-process binder that conforms to the s-c-s binder SPI so user modules can be wired and exercised without Redis/Rabbit/etc.
Implement helpers to bind and apply @ConfigurationProperties from arbitrary property sources so different combinations of props can be tested easily.
Implement Hamcrest matchers to assert messages/payloads received from the in-memory binder.
Write unit and integration tests for the new test support, plus reference documentation and a sample module test.
Study YARN ApplicationMaster / Container IPC, existing s-c-d YARN integration, and derive a YARNModuleDeployer SPI suitable for distributed module placement.
Produce a design document defining the YARNModuleDeployer interface, lifecycle hooks, and how the s-c-d YARN deployer will use it.
Implement a minimal end-to-end prototype of the YARNModuleDeployer SPI that can launch a module container on a YARN cluster.
Analyze the existing Spring XD trigger (source) module and port it into the s-c-s repo using s-c-s source module conventions.
Add unit/integration tests for the ported trigger module and document its usage in a streaming pipeline.
Investigate Spring Data Redis cluster topology (Lettuce), Sentinel failover, and design how s-c-s exposes cluster and Sentinel as bus options.
Implement cluster and Sentinel support on top of the existing Redis binder, including configuration properties and connection factory wiring.
Add tests for cluster and Sentinel scenarios (failover, re-routing) and document how to configure stream and batch pipelines against a Redis cluster.
Review upstream Receptor API changes and update the s-c-d receptor-client to comply with the latest API.
Update and add tests for the upgraded receptor-client, including compatibility checks against the new server.

Design how module definition parameters (name, count, properties, etc.) are passed into YARN containers and made available to the running module.
